origins: When a body or mind limits what we can do, tasks that were easy become hard and we depend on others. Over time, “I need help with some things” can become “I am helpless.”
teaches: “God is our refuge and strength, an ever-present help in times of trouble.” “The LORD is my helper; I will not be afraid.” “I can do all things through Christ who gives me strength.” Even when we need much help from others, we still have prayer, love, wisdom, and presence to give, and we are never helpless before God: “You hold my right hand.” Dependence is part of how God made us all.
errors: Believing I am either independent or helpless.
Predicting that I will never be capable.
Feeling dependent and concluding that I am helpless.
questions: What can I still do, even if differently?
What aids or adaptations could increase my independence?
What can I give to others?
What does God say about helping those who depend on Him?
Who helps me, and what do they receive from helping?
What is one task I can reclaim?
truth: I am not helpless. I can do many things, in my own way and with help. God is my helper, and I have much to give.
hw_truths: God is my refuge and strength.
I can do all things through Christ.
log: Each week, note one thing you did yourself and one thing you gave.
actions: Say it when you feel helpless.
prayer: Lord, I feel helpless. You are my helper. Show me what I can still do, send practical help, and let me give from where I am. Amen.
